info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Habakkuk

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Genius of Electricity

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Sir Isaac Newton
info_cards.fact: "To every action there is always an equal and opposite reaction." — English physicist and mathematician whose laws of motion form the basis of classical mechanics.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Archimedes
info_cards.fact: "Give me a place to stand, and a lever long enough, and I will move the world." — Ancient Greek mathematician and inventor known for his work on levers, buoyancy, and geometry.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Euclid
info_cards.fact: "The laws of nature are but the mathematical thoughts of God." — Ancient Greek mathematician often called the 'father of geometry' for his work Elements.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Pythagoras
info_cards.fact: "There is geometry in the humming of the strings." — Ancient Greek mathematician and philosopher credited with the Pythagorean theorem about right triangles.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Al-Khwarizmi
info_cards.fact: "The work of the mathematician... is to clarify what is necessary in the science of computation." — Persian mathematician whose works introduced algebra and gave us the term 'algorithm.'

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Ibn al-Haytham
info_cards.fact: "The seeker after truth is not one who studies the writings of the ancients... and then makes them his guide." — Arab scientist often called the 'father of modern optics' for his experimental studies of light and vision.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Avicenna (Ibn Sina)
info_cards.fact: "The world is divided into men who have wit and no religion, and men who have religion and no wit." — Persian physician and philosopher whose medical encyclopedia, The Canon of Medicine, was used for centuries.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Hypatia of Alexandria
info_cards.fact: "Reserve your right to think, for even to think wrongly is better than not to think at all." — Greek mathematician and astronomer in Alexandria, one of the earliest known female scholars in mathematics.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Emmy Noether
info_cards.fact: "If one proves the equality of two numbers... by establishing a one-to-one correspondence between them... this is mathematics." — German mathematician whose theorem connecting symmetry and conservation laws transformed physics and algebra.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: John von Neumann
info_cards.fact: "There's no sense in being precise when you don't even know what you're talking about." — Hungarian-American mathematician who made major contributions to computing, game theory, and quantum mechanics.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Srinivasa Ramanujan
info_cards.fact: "An equation for me has no meaning unless it expresses a thought of God." — Indian mathematician who, with little formal training, made extraordinary contributions to number theory.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Carl Friedrich Gauss
info_cards.fact: "Mathematics is the queen of the sciences." — German mathematician who made major contributions to number theory, statistics, and astronomy.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Blaise Pascal
info_cards.fact: "The heart has its reasons which reason does not know." — French mathematician and philosopher who contributed to probability theory and built an early calculating machine.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Rene Descartes
info_cards.fact: "I think, therefore I am." — French philosopher and mathematician who developed the Cartesian coordinate system linking algebra and geometry.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Leonhard Euler
info_cards.fact: "Logic is the foundation of the certainty of all the knowledge we acquire." — Swiss mathematician who introduced much of modern mathematical notation and made discoveries across many fields.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Florence Bascom
info_cards.fact: "There is yet work to do." — American geologist who became one of the first women to earn a Ph.D. in geology and to work for the U.S. Geological Survey.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Mary Anning
info_cards.fact: "The world has used me so unkindly, I fear it has made me suspicious of everyone." — English fossil collector whose discoveries of marine reptile fossils helped found modern paleontology.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Charles Lyell
info_cards.fact: "No causes whatever have, from the earliest time to which we can look back, to the present, ever acted, but those now acting." — Scottish geologist whose ideas about gradual geological change influenced Charles Darwin's theory of evolution.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Alfred Wegener
info_cards.fact: "Scientists still do not appear to understand sufficiently that all earth sciences must contribute evidence toward unveiling the state of our planet." — German scientist who proposed the theory of continental drift, a forerunner to plate tectonics.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Inge Lehmann
info_cards.fact: "You should know how many idiots there are in the world... if you are interested in science." — Danish seismologist who discovered the Earth's solid inner core using earthquake data.
